statement: Normalizing a lead's email before validating it is sufficient, even when the original email violates the normalization rule.
evidence_of_dependence: expr='LOWER(TRIM(email))'; the WHERE clause validates LOWER(TRIM(email)) rather than requiring email = LOWER(TRIM(email)).
alternative: The lead contract explicitly assigns "on_failure: delete_row" to the rule "email = LOWER(TRIM(email))", which supports rejecting non-normalized source emails instead of retaining corrected ones.
reason: This changes which leads survive staging and therefore changes downstream lead populations.

statement: Every non-null program_id in raw.marketo_campaign already matches the required Marketo identifier format.
evidence_of_dependence: ('program_id','program_id','VARCHAR') is projected with CAST, without format validation or nullification.
alternative: The campaign contract requires "program_id IS NULL OR program_id ~ '^MAR[0-9]+$'" and specifies "on_failure: nullify_field".
reason: Unvalidated identifiers could violate the staging contract and alter downstream program attribution.

statement: The is_most_recent_version column does not need to be supplied by the email-template-history staging model.
evidence_of_dependence: The email-template projection includes version, operational, subject, and from_email, but does not project is_most_recent_version.
alternative: The email-template-history contract explicitly lists "name: is_most_recent_version" with "data_type: BOOLEAN".
reason: Omitting a contracted column can prevent downstream consumers from selecting the current template version.

statement: The active field in raw.marketo_campaign contains no null values.
evidence_of_dependence: ('is_active','active','BOOLEAN') is handled by CAST(active AS BOOLEAN), with no COALESCE.
alternative: The campaign contract requires "is_active = COALESCE(is_active, FALSE)" and describes the correction as "Default NULL active flag to FALSE".
reason: Any null source flag would remain null instead of becoming the required non-null false value.

statement: Each raw email-template-history row already has a non-null version.
evidence_of_dependence: ('version','version','DOUBLE') is projected, while where remains empty for this model.
alternative: The email-template-history contract specifies "constraints: [not_null]" for version.
reason: A null source version would pass through despite being essential to the contracted template-version grain.

statement: The staging models may expose their created_timestamp, updated_timestamp, and campaign recurrence timestamps as VARCHAR rather than TIMESTAMP.
evidence_of_dependence: All four model definitions include ('created_timestamp','created_at','VARCHAR') and ('updated_timestamp','updated_at','VARCHAR'); campaigns also includes ('recurrence_start_at','recurrence_start_at','VARCHAR').
alternative: The staging governance specifies "timestamp_format: TIMESTAMP", supporting typed timestamps rather than strings.
reason: This affects timestamp columns across four staging models and can change downstream date comparisons and calculations.

statement: An email send's email_send_id is the raw send activity's id, without any additional derivation.
evidence_of_dependence: The send-email projection maps both ('activity_id','id','VARCHAR') and ('email_send_id','id','VARCHAR').
reason: If email_send_id denotes a different business key, downstream send attribution or joins could use the wrong grain.

statement: Each email_template_id referenced by a send matches at most one row in staging.stg_marketo__email_template_history.
alternative: The staging contract defines the history grain as "One row per email template version", allowing multiple rows per template, while the email-sends contract specifies "One row per email_send_id".
reason: Multiple matching versions multiply send rows and consequently inflate engagement metrics throughout downstream marts.

statement: Every lead-and-day group in the change events contains at least one matching metadata row with a non-null rest_name_xf.
evidence_of_dependence: LOWER(d.rest_name_xf) AS field_name ... BOOL_OR(field_name='email') AS email_c
alternative: The contract explicitly allows unmatched metadata and says "NULL primary_attribute_column never matches; groups may have all flags FALSE", whereas an all-null BOOL_OR input produces NULL.
reason: Entirely unmatched groups would produce null flags instead of the required false flags.

statement: A missing or null field-change flag should be treated as false when determining SCD backfill boundaries.
alternative: The SCD contract says a group continues only when "the field value is null and the corresponding details flag is false"; it does not explicitly equate a missing or null flag with false.
reason: This interpretation can carry values across boundaries that a strict false-only interpretation would retain.

statement: For each lead and day, no two distinct primary_attribute_value_id values map to the same tracked REST attribute token with conflicting selected old_value values.
reason: If multiple attribute IDs map to the same token, MAX selects by string value rather than by the earliest change for that target attribute.

statement: Each non-null created_timestamp used by the lead calendar spine begins with a valid YYYY-MM-DD representation of its intended creation date.
alternative: The contract requires using "the date portion of created_timestamp" without specifying that the date always occupies its first ten characters.
reason: Other valid timestamp representations could silently exclude leads or assign an incorrect start date.

statement: Exactly one history row per email_template_id is marked is_most_recent_version.
reason: Missing or multiple current-version flags would omit templates or violate the required one-row-per-template grain.

statement: The staged lead base contains at most one row per lead_id.
evidence_of_dependence: SELECT l.* ... FROM staging.stg_marketo__lead l LEFT JOIN deleted d USING(lead_id)
alternative: The intermediate lead contract explicitly notes that "duplicates on lead_id are preserved", so downstream uniqueness cannot be inferred from that intermediate model.
reason: The mart preserves base duplicates despite requiring exactly one row per lead.

statement: The calendar-spine-to-SCD join produces at most one row per lead_id and date_day.
evidence_of_dependence: FROM spine s LEFT JOIN changes c ON s.lead_id=c.lead_id AND s.date_day=c.valid_to
alternative: The SCD contract states "no enforced uniqueness" and "multiple rows may exist for a lead and date", while the lead calendar spine preserves source duplicates.
reason: Duplicate matches violate the daily history grain and make the descending-date partition boundaries ambiguous.

statement: Leads with no email engagement may be assigned the rfm_segment 'Inactive' rather than 'Unknown'.
evidence_of_dependence: Segmentation runs over metrics after the left join and zero defaults, with "ELSE 'Inactive' END AS rfm_segment".
alternative: The contract says to derive segmentation from aggregated engagement and specifies "rfm_segment defaults to \"Unknown\" ... when segmentation is missing".
reason: Every eligible lead without engagement receives a different segment under this interpretation.

statement: A missing or unparseable lead creation date may be represented by a lead_tenure_days value of zero.
alternative: The contract defines tenure as "the calendar days between the lead's created date and today" and supplies no zero fallback for missing or invalid creation dates.
reason: The fallback makes unknown tenure indistinguishable from a lead created today.

statement: All creation and last-engagement dates used by eligible leads are on or before the execution date.
evidence_of_dependence: DATE_DIFF('day',CAST(last_email_sent_at AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) and DATE_DIFF('day',TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(created_timestamp,1,10) AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) are returned without a lower bound.
reason: Future source dates would produce negative values despite the contracted nonnegative tests.
